phantom rider carson.name: Phantom Rider (Carson)
phantom rider carson.origin: Banker Carson was a banker in Caliber City, Texas during the days of the American Frontier. Seeking riches, he developed the costumed identity of the Phantom Rider to rob stage coaches. He found the opportunity for a fall guy from a local rancher named Haverill whose son Sandy required a $1000 medical treatment on his leg. When Carson denied giving Haverill a loan in his capacity as a banker, Haverill vowed to get the money for his son's treatment no matter what. Carson sent a message to Haverill offering him a means to treat his son. Instead, Haverill witnessed the Phantom Rider rob a coach. The Rider then threatened to kill Haverill's son if he did not agree to help stash the stolen loot. With no other choice, Haverill agreed. Eventually, the Texas Kid began investigating the robberies and caught Haverill collecting the stolen money. Learning about how Haverill was forced to collect the stolen money and shown the blackmail notes written by the Phantom Rider, the Texas Kid agreed to help Haverill. Having Haverill turned over to the police, Banker Carson was very vocal in implicating Haverill as the Phantom Rider. The Texas Kid then came back disguised as the Phantom Rider and informed them that Haverill was not the outlaw. Shocked to see someone posing as his alter ego, Carson blew his cover by denouncing the "Phantom Rider" as an impostor. The Texas Kid revealed his trick and outed Carson as the Phantom Rider. Carson confessed to his crimes and tried to shoot the Texas Kid but was easily disarmed. Carson was turned over to the sheriff, his subsequent fate is unknown.
weapons: He carried a six gun.

phantome.name: Phantome
phantome.origin: Phantome was an inventor that wanted to bring justice to the streets. So, she created a machine she believed could take a person's powers and give them to her, though it actually copied them. She first copied the powers of someone with electrical powers. She then targeted Vengeance. With help from her partner Gargantua, Phantome lured in Vengeance and managed to copy his powers, becoming a Ghost Rider-like being. However, instead of targeting people who hurt people, Phantome targeted people for minor crimes. When Vengeance saw what Phantome was doing on television, he went to stop her and was aided by Gargantua who was shocked by Phantome's actions. The pair confronted Phantome, and Phantone engaged Vengenace in a fight. That was when Vengeance discovered that Phantome had only copied his powers, not stole them. Eventually, Vengeance convinced Phantone that her actions were wrong, and they worked together to put out a fire caused by their fight. To prevent the fire from spreading, Phantome rode her motorcycle into some burning fuel tanks.
powers: Ghost Rider-like Transformation and Hellfire Kiss: A burning kiss Phantome could release that could kill someone instantly.
weapons: Burning whip.

phao.name: Phao
phao.origin: Phao was a slave driver under the rule of King Cheops during his reign between 2589 to 2566 BC. He forced slaves to construct the pyramids in the region. One day, his work was interrupted by 1940s time traveler Tommy Tyme who came to Egypt to learn why the pyramids were being build. Phao, thinking the boy to be an uppity slave, attacked him only to find the Brooklyn native fighting back with his sling shot. Pulled away by the slave, Tommy was forced to assist in placing the final blocks on the pyramid being constructed. Phao then ordered the slaves to get started on the next pyramid only to have Tommy start a rebellion. During the fight, Phao grabbed Tommy and dragged him into the pyramid that was to be the tomb for his ruler. There, he intended to force Tommy into a sarcophagus to suffocate. Tommy fought his way free and trapped Phao and his men inside instead before returning to his own town, having gotten the answer he sought. Phao's subsequent fate is unknown, though it's unlikely he would be alive in modern times.
weapons: Phao drove his slaves with a whip and also carried a dagger.

phehemenes.name: Phehemenes
phehemenes.origin: Phehemenes was king of Zingara, and ruled from Kordava. He was married to Sharmela, fifteen years his junior. His rule was troubled by the civil wars orchestrated by the princelings of Zingara in attempts to overthrow him. He was also aware that Sharmela was unfaithful to him, including her being the lover of Captain Bar-Helm of Phehemenes' army, and that both conspired against Phehemenes. He kept Sharmela at her side both for the spice it induced in his life and because the populace would think ill of him for having chosen her. A princeling, Ragnok was defeated by Conan of Cimmeria, a mercenary into Phehemenes' army. According to Conan, Phehemenes, unlike most kings, would simply jail Ragnok for some time in order to ensure peace, before releasing him. In gratitude for his actions, Phehemenes ordered the servant-girl Nefertali to place herself at Conan's disposal. As he and Sharmela received Conan at court to express their gratitude, Ragnok "broke free" (in fact freed by Bar-Helm) and attempted to slay Phehemenes, but was killed in duel with Conan. Bar-Helm and Sharmela then decided to eliminate Conan in order to more easily attain the king. After killing Bar-Helm, Conan was stopped from hurting Sharmela by Phehemenes who confessed his knowledge of the conspirators and decided to have the event hidden. Sick of it, Conan preferred to withdrew from Phehemenes' services.
weaknesses: Phehemenes' only waknessesses were allegedly his craving for a hookah of kif/hashish at bedtime and his obsessive love for his bride.

phelch.name: Phelch
phelch.origin: Phelch was a member of an ancient race of sentient vegetables. Overcoming the limits of their roots, the vegetables evolved into space-spanning overachievers. Unfortunately they met their doom when, in their vanity, they failed to pick themselves at the first cosmic frost. Phelch, in the form of a turnip, was the sole survivor and wandered the trackless void of space for eons, searching for a more efficient body to frame its superior intellect and incomparable power. Phelch eventually crash-landed on Earth in Cleveland, Ohio where, although the bulk of it was burnt up in the atmosphere, it encountered Arthur Winslow. Phelch convinced Winslow to allow a merger, enabling him to become the super-hero he had always wanted to be. As Turnip-Man, he saved the lives of the passengers of a bus which had driven off of a bridge as a result of a scuffle between Howard the Duck and the Kidney Lady. When Winslow's friend and roommate, Beverly Switzler, recognized him, Phelch took over their combined form in order to experience physical pleasure. The Space Turnip grabbed Beverly and took her to Sunset Slope. Howard, following advice from the Kidney Lady, tracked them down and confronted the Space Turnip in battle. Howard, figuring out that "the brains are in the greens," tore the leaves and stem off of Turnip-Man. The Space Turnip then pulled Howard high into the air, planning to drop and kill him, but Howard succeeded in maneuvering it too close to a smokestack, where it was destroyed.

Unfortunately they met their doom when, in their vanity, they failed to pick themselves at the first cosmic frost. Phelch, in the form of a turnip, was the sole survivor and wandered the trackless void of space for eons, searching for a more efficient body to frame its superior intellect and incomparable power. Phelch eventually crash-landed on Earth in Cleveland, Ohio where, although the bulk of it was burnt up in the atmosphere, it encountered Arthur Winslow. Phelch convinced Winslow to allow a merger, enabling him to become the super-hero he had always wanted to be. As Turnip-Man, he saved the lives of the passengers of a bus which had driven off of a bridge as a result of a scuffle between Howard the Duck and the Kidney Lady. When Winslow's friend and roommate, Beverly Switzler, recognized him, Phelch took over their combined form in order to experience physical pleasure. The Space Turnip grabbed Beverly and took her to Sunset Slope. Howard, following advice from the Kidney Lady, tracked them down and confronted the Space Turnip in battle. Howard, figuring out that "the brains are in the greens," tore the leaves and stem off of Turnip-Man. The Space Turnip then pulled Howard high into the air, planning to drop and kill him, but Howard succeeded in maneuvering it too close to a smokestack, where it was destroyed.

phentoh.name: Phentoh
phentoh.first_appearance: Rise of the Black Panther Vol 1 2
phentoh.origin: Phentoh was one of the handful of Wakandans abducted by the Atlantean scientist U-Man and General Zoruun of the Nigandan Army during a period of roughly a decade to perform studies on them. Due to the strange nature of their disappearance, then-King S'Yan decided to keep the incidents a secret from the public to avoid panic. When T'Challa succeeded S'Yan, he learned of these incidents and acted on them. He eventually located the base of the kidnappers in Niganda and shut down their operations with the help of the Atlantean king Namor. Phentoh and the other abductees were then brought back to Wakanda. Not long afterwards, Erik Killmonger tracked down several of the former abductees, and brutally murdered them since he believed their lives were sullied because they allowed themselves to be taken alive from Wakanda. Phentoh was one of his victims. Killmonger additionally used a device of his own invention to obtain their memories and gain any knowledge they possessed that could be of use for him.

phil bradshaw.name: Phil Bradshaw
phil bradshaw.origin: Phil Bradshaw was a Maggia-affiliated individual known for hosting elaborate social events that served as a cover for criminal gatherings. Among his possessions was a valuable painting, which was later stolen by the Black Cat during a burglary carried out without immediate interference. At a later time, Bradshaw hosted a costume party attended by numerous associates connected to his operations. During the event, the Black Cat deliberately revealed to him that she had taken the painting, prompting a violent response. When Spider-Man intervened, a firefight broke out between Bradshaw’s men and the hero. As the confrontation unfolded and his forces were subdued, Bradshaw attempted to escape the premises. However, he was intercepted and taken into custody by Captain DeWolff and accompanying police officers, bringing the incident to an end.

Fox eventually uncovered information on Cage that was not known to the public. Fox got drunk and told Flea about Noah Burstein's prison experiments which gave Cage his super powers. This information gave Flea leverage to send Cage back to jail. Fox was later murdered. In the aftermath of Phil Fox's death, Big Ben Donovan witnessed Mrs. Jenks' confession to the murder of the reporter, even though she didn't kill him. Fox's murderer was actually Billy Bob Rackham. Mrs. Jenks confessed just before she died to clear Cage's then-girlfriend, Claire Temple of the charges.

phil rodriguez.name: Phil Rodriguez
phil rodriguez.origin: Phil Rodriguez was a NYPD Detective when a new Spider-Woman began to ravage the city streets, causing several people to disappear. His boss, Captain Ronald Parady, pressed him to investigate the case. After speaking with the officer who investigated the complaint about Spider-Woman, Phil knew she had been seen near a house owned by Andrew Ramsey, one of the first missing, so he hurried to the spot. When he arrived at the house in Greenwich Village, he saw Jessica Drew coming out through the front door, pursued by the new Spider-Woman. Phil shot her, who escaped to the roof taking Mattie Franklin with her. Spider-Man, who was also investigating the events, faced Spider-Woman, but she controlled him easily and left him motionless while carrying Mattie there. When Phil and Jessica were able to get to the roof where Spider-Woman was found, she was lying unconscious on the floor, and Mattie had absorbed her powers. Mattie could not control the newly acquired powers, and the spider legs on her back appeared for the first time, hitting Jessica Drew and attacking Spider-Man. Phil fired at the legs, making Mattie release Spider-Man, but the girl then fled, driven by the legs over which she had no control. Jessica and Phil then ran to the place where they had left Spider-Woman handcuffed but found that the handcuffs were broken and she was gone. While trying to find clues to discover how she had been freed, Dr. Octopus appeared accompanied by Mattie, now under mind control. Phil fired at Doc Ock, but his metal tentacles deflected the bullets. Thankfully, Madame Web, who had accompanied the heroes, managed to break the control exercised by Spider-Woman over Mattie, and the heroes quickly arrested Doctor Octopus. Phil lamented the paperwork that awaited him and, to make matters worse, Spider-Man and Mattie disappeared before he could stop them. Soon after, Madame Web explained to Phil what they knew about the origin of the powers Mattie had received. Now that Madame Web's granddaughter had lost her powers, Phil agreed to leave at her expense as she had not been responsible for the deaths she had caused and was assured that this would help her recover.

philip cho.name: Philip Cho
philip cho.origin: ===Early Life=== Philip Cho was born in South Korea. When he found a job in the United States, he and his wife Helen moved together to Tucson, Arizona. They bought a house in Tucson, and integrated well with the already existing community. Philip and Helen had quite a passion for historical names, something they showed the moment they had to name their two children Helen gave birth to. Their first child was a son, Amadeus Cho, named after the composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and their second child was a daughter, Maddy, named after the physicist Marie Curie, she is called Maddie for short. The Cho's lived a normal and happy life, but Amadeus showed from his very childhood that he was different: he was incredibly smart for such a young boy, and learnt a lot of things by himself, becoming highly cultured and increasing his already remarkable intelligence. Philip supported his genius son, and tried to go along with his talent. The more Amadeus grew up, the more his parents realized he was a genius. When the boy was fifteen years old, the soap corporation Excello, announced an online game to reward young geniuses, a quiz show named Brain Fight. Amadeus participated, and he easily won the $5,000 reward, placing first. Philip and Helen of course were happy for their son's results, but they didn't know this was just the beginning of the end for their family. The person who had organized Brain Fight, in fact, was another genius and former child prodigy, Pythagoras Dupree, whose real aim was to search the world for other people whose intellect might rival his own… and to eliminate them as unwanted rivals. By winning his game, Amadeus Cho had been awarded with the title of Mastermind Excello and the position of “7th Smartest Man in the World” (Pythagoras, by his own claim, was the 6th), and that was more than enough of a reason to kill him. Dupree had his men attack Amadeus' house, and in the following explosion, Philip and his wife were killed. ===Underworld=== Amadeus became the best friend of the Greek demigod Hercules, and accompanied him in many of his adventures: during a mission to save Zeus from the Hades (Underworld), while Hercules battled hordes of vengeful enemies in Tartarus, Amadeus ended up in the Elysian Fields (the Greek version of Heaven), where he met his parents again. Before he could finish apologizing for having "caused" their deaths by winning Brain Fight, Philip and Helen interrupted him and hugged him, happy and proud of what their son had become. Before he went back to Earth, however, Helen told Amadeus something he didn't know yet: Maddy didn't die in the explosion, and was still alive, taken by the Excello and kept somewhere, needing his help. He couldn't do much else but watch over his children from the Fields of Elysian. It was now up to Amadeus to make things right and to reunite with what remained of his family.

philip gavin.name: Philip Gavin
philip gavin.origin: Philip Gavin was Assistant Director of the secret service organization MI5. Gavin, however, had ambitions to become the next director of the organization. As such, when he learned of a potential terrorist attack on the city of London by R.A.I.D., he decided not to tell anyone in an attempt to force the then director of MI5 to resign after the fallout from the incident. After other agents discovered the terrorist threat, Gavin was forced to take action, assembling a team that he felt would fail in its mission led by Union Jack. Union Jack and the ad hoc group of heroes did succeed in stopping the terrorist threat, however, with the city's casualties numbering over two hundred, instead of in the thousands. This still had the effect of forcing the director to resign, thereby realizing Gavin's dreams. Union Jack, however, put the pieces together and discovered Gavin's plot, confronting the would-be director in his office. Gavin threatened to cut Jack's MI5 support if he didn't go along with his machinations, prompting Union Jack to punch him in the face and haul him in front of the British media to confess his crimes. Gavin's subsequent fate is as yet unrevealed.

philip hockney.name: Philip Hockney
philip hockney.origin: Philip Hockney was the C.E.O. of the Chemaxone Corporation, one of the corporations that attended the secret meeting called by Aleksander Lukin at the Kronas Building with the intent of selling the Cosmic Cube to the highest bidder. When the purchase figures became significant, Hockney asked if what he was selling was indeed a real Cosmic Cube and that he should at least demonstrate what it was capable of. Lukin calmly asked if he was the leader of those who had previously rejected his offer to acquire his corporation, and when Hockney confirmed, Lukin using the power of the Cosmic Cube had each of the C.E.O.'s sign a merger agreement for their corporations to become subsidiaries of the Kronas Corporation. Then in a mocking manner, Lukin asked Hockney if he was satisfied with the demonstration, and Hockney servilely replied "yes, yes sir, Mr. Lukin".

philip russell.name: Philip Russell
philip russell.origin: Philip Russoff was a young nobleman in Transylvania where he met and started dating an American college student named Laura. However, Laura left him when she met and eventually married his older brother Baron Gregory Russoff. After the wedding, Philip moved to America and changed his name to Philip Russell. Years later, after Laura and her children Jacob and Lissa moved to America after Gregory became a werewolf and could not guarantee their safety, Philip and Laura met again. After Gregory was killed by werewolf hunters, Philip and Laura married, and Laura and her children moved into Philip's home in Los Angeles. Philip and Laura did not tell Jacob (now known as Jack) and Lissa that Philip was their uncle, and they only knew him as a stepfather. Years later, after Laura had been injured in an auto accident, Jack suspected that Philip had conspired with members of the Committee to have her killed, to inherit the Russoff fortune that she had inherited from Gregory. Laura died soon after, but not before making her son vow not to harm Philip. Philip was taken prisoner by Taboo in a plot to get Jack Russell to reveal the location of the Darkhold. He left Philip to be killed by his nephew who had always sought revenge for his mother's death. Jack, however, remembered the vow he had made to his mother and used his werewolf powers to break them out instead. When they confronted Taboo, Philip's mind was transferred into the body of Algon, the wizard's son. After he was freed, Phillip revealed that he was in fact Jack and Lissa's paternal uncle and that he was not involved in Laura's death - he had been trying to help after she was blackmailed by the Committee.

philip wing.name: Philip Wing
philip wing.origin: ===20th Century=== thumb|left|Philip Wing pre-transformation The Man With No Face was a Chinese citizen by the name of Philip Wing. In the 1950s he became a spy for communist China and was sent to the United States. There he developed the identity of the Man With No Face and forced the citizens of New York's Chinatown to send money to China to support their efforts in the Cold War for fear of their family members back home being harmed in retaliation. Those threatened included his own brother, Howard, who was a police officer in the Chinatown district who had no idea that his own brother was the Man With No Face. thumb|119px|Man With No Face, circa 1954 Officer Wing called in the assistance of Captain America (William Burnside) and Bucky (Jack Monroe) to assist him in the capture of the Man With No Face. Captain America chased the Man With No Face across the rooftops of Chinatown and overpowered him in hand-to-hand combat. Wing then revealed to Captain America his true identity, and choosing death over capture jumped off a building to his seeming demise. The fall disfigured his face rendering him unrecognizable and Captain America decided to keep Philip's true identity a secret from his brother. However, it appeared that the Man With No Face survived the fall and was brought back to China where he was subjected to experiments by the Chinese in their attempt to create their own super-soldier. Though he gained phasing abilities, he was considered a failure and was used more as a spy. He was in service to Professor Zhang Chin, a scientist who believed that Earth's growing population would put a great strain on their ecosystem. The Man With No Face defended Chin when the Winter Soldier came to assassinate him. He was able to escape, failing at his mission. ===Modern Age=== Surviving to the modern age, the Man With No Face was involved in a plan to capture the remains of the original Human Torch. Chin was planning on using his unique DNA and cell structure to create a virus to eradicate half the planet's population. The mercenary, Batroc the Leaper had stolen a number of UN computers pertaining to their target, but ran into interference. The Man With No Face recognized the Winter Soldier from Batroc's photographs, who was now the current Captain America. Eager for a rematch, the Man With No Face fought against his opponent while Batroc's mercenaries retrieved their quarry. However, the Man With No Face was forced to flee when he was shot in the back by Black Widow. The Man With No Face reappeared in China to protect his master, knowing that Bucky and his allies would try to stop them. In the ensuring fight, Chin died from a heart attack. Shocked at the death of his leader, the Man With No Face unknowingly rendered himself vulnerable while touching his body, as Namor snapped his neck, seemingly killing him.

philips waggoner.name: Philips Waggoner
philips waggoner.species: Human transformed into a giant Wendigo
philips waggoner.origin: Philips Waggoner was a miner who went on an expedition funded by the Roxxon Corporation to find the site where the Avingnon Party ate each other during their last seven weeks of life stranded in an improvised shelter due to a blizzard. Unbeknownst to Waggoner and the archaeologist Dr. Ella Sterling, they were to be used by Roxxon executive Mr. Banks in the Ur-Wendigo experiment, which aimed at creating a far more powerful version of the Wendigo by making a person eat Wendigo flesh at said site due to its cursed nature. thumb|left|Human form After the team was dropped in the Canadian wilderness, Waggoner noticed the rations case was nowhere to be found and warned the others. Luckily for the team, Weapon H overheard their conversation and killed a deer to provide them food; Waggoner, however, didn't eat its meat because Mr. Banks convinced him it could be poisoned. Once Dr. Sterling managed to locate the site, Waggoner was tricked into eating Wendigo meat by Mr. Banks and turned into the Ur-Wendigo. When Mr. Banks tried to feed Dr. Sterling to the creature, Weapon H came out of the shadows and attacked it. Weapon H tried to take Dr. Sterling to safety afterwards, but the Ur-Wendigo caught him mid-air and took a bite of him, getting bigger than before. As it was about to eat Weapon H whole, Doctor Strange burst onto the scene to take the creature down with his enchanted arrows; however, they didn't have any effect on it due to its hardened hide. To finally put an end to the Ur-Wendigo, Weapon H allowed himself to be eaten so he could use Doctor Strange's axe to kill the creature from within.
powers: Wendigo physiology, but far greater due to the curse having undergone a multiplier effect. In addition, Waggoner was able to grow larger whenever he ate flesh.

phillip children of heaven.name: Phillip (Children of Heaven)
phillip children of heaven.origin: thumb|left|135px Phillip, a seemingly kindly mutant, led the Children of Heaven cult, ostensibly a sanctuary for runaway teens, especially mutants. In reality, Phillip used his cultists to perform various shady deals, including those in pornography and drugs, using force when they would not oblige him. Archangel, who followed a drug deal back to the cult, fought off the group, a battle which ended when Beth, one of the most victimized cultists, sent a psychic bolt through Phillip's head. Phillip was taken into custody by the police. It is unknown if he retained his mutant powers after the event of M-Day.
powers: Phillip's mutant ability allowed him to enter the minds of other people. Mind Reading: Phillip has the power to read people's thoughts. Mental Replay: Phillip has the power to make others experience their deepest fears.

phillip telepath.name: Phillip (Telepath)
phillip telepath.origin: Phillip was an unknowing telepathic mutant who moved to Los Angeles, California, to be closer to his sons and ex-wife after losing his job. He was among the many LA citizens who fell under the thrall of Cassandra Nova and joined her Owl Cult while she possessed the body of the teenage mutant Ginny Guzman, who possessed the ability to instill a sense of belonging in others. Cassandra intended to initiate the Great Corruption, the merger of the physical world and the Astral Plane, which would enable all the world's Mummudrai to gain physical bodies and slaughter humanity. To do this, she was required to sacrifice a telepath on the full moon. While calmly reassuring Phil that he had a place with her society, she beheaded him with a sword. Cassandra placed Phil's severed head within a ritual circle, opening the gate to the Astral Plane.
powers: Phil was a latent telepathic mutant, unaware of his powers until moments before he died. He himself believed his powers were simple headaches.

phillip barnett.name: Phillip Barnett
phillip barnett.origin: Phillip Barnett was an employee of Justin Hammer. He helped his employer hijack Iron Man's armor. Phillip developed a computer system which could neutralize the controls of Iron Man Armor Model 4 and manipulate its actions. Tony Stark thought that the armor was simply malfunctioning. When Tony Stark was kidnapped by Hammer, Phillip was tasked with opening his briefcase, which secretly contained the Iron Man armor, but failed. When Hammer's plan to defeat Iron Man in his Villa failed and it sunk in the process, Iron Man rescued Barnett from drowning, and later forced him to testify against Hammer in order to clean his name for the things he was forced to do when his suit was hijacked, like murdering ambassor Sergei Kotzinin. When the Scorpion was hired by his boss, he questioned his capability to work out. When the Scorpion eventually failed to accomplish his task, Phillip witnessed Hammer enlisting other operatives to bring him back.

phillip blackwood.origin: thumb|left|300px|Phillip in his "Demon of the Deep" costume Phillip Blackwood was a wealthy yacht owner that operated in the South-Sea of China during the 1940s. He caused one of his cousin's boats, carrying a load of pearls, to sink in the hopes of getting salvage rights to the cache of pearls. However, he had to frighten off competition from American diver Dave Dean and Chinese salvager Wing Po. To this end, he created a demonic looking diving suit and dove down into the wreck to ward off those who would seek to salvage the pearls. He gained a reputation of "Demon of the Deep". Encountering Dave Dean underwater, Phillip cut his air hose, forcing him to rush up to the surface and be stricken with the bends. While Dean blamed Wing Po for the attack, Phillip went down once again as the the "Demon of the Deep" and slew one of Po's divers. Going down to investigate further, Dean managed to knock out the "Demon" and bring him to the surface, revealing him as Phillip Blackwood. Phillip was taken to the authorities to stand for his crimes. His fate is unrevealed.
weapons: When underwater as the "Demon of the Deep", Phillip was armed with a knife.

He was eventually killed by an overdose of a mystical drug, Darklight, developed by D'Spayre.

phillip chambers.name: Phillip Chambers
phillip chambers.first_appearance: Spider-Man, Punisher, Sabretooth: Designer Genes Vol 1 1
phillip chambers.origin: Phillip Chambers was a genetic scientist, formerly employed by Canada's Department K, and may have been one of the people who experimented on Sabretooth, Wolverine, and Silver Fox. At some point, he left government work and switched to the private sector, being employed by Roxxon to produce animal/human hybrids. Using his own brother, Mitchell Chambers, as a test subject, he was able to successfully create a hybrid of human and animal traits – though the result lacked any human intelligence or identity. Needing more test subjects and genetic samples to continue his research, Dr. Chambers sent his now animalistic brother to gather the required materials. This brought his work to the attention of Spider-Man, the Punisher, and Sabretooth himself, with the latter recognizing his work as similar to the experiments that had been performed on him in the past. When the three of them broke into his lab, Phillip unleashed his brother against them while he made his escape. While he was able to delay Spider-Man and the Punisher, he was unable to elude Sabretooth, who killed the scientist.

phillip durant.name: Phillip Durant
phillip durant.species: Human possessed by Jack the Ripper
phillip durant.origin: Phillip Durant was the lover of Fah Lo Suee, daughter of Fu Manchu. To get revenge on his daughter, Fu Manchu had organized Jack the Ripper to possess Phillip. Some years afterwards, Phillip began copying the Ripper by murdering women in the Whitechapel area of London. He soon clashed with Shang Chi, Leiko Wu and Clive Reston, and was overpowered by Shang Chi. Fah Lo Suee intervened, hoping she could restore Phillip to himself, but he attacked her and she shot him, killing him.
powers: Durant was treated with an elixir that extended his lifespan and increased his durability.
weaknesses: Durant was reprogrammed with the insanity of Jack the Ripper, and felt a psychological compulsion to kill women.

phillip garcia.name: Phillip Garcia
phillip garcia.origin: Philip originally posed as his brother Ramon the original Senor Muerte. Working with Tarantula he planned to smuggle Madbomb parts. Their plot was uncovered by Ken Astor who under the alias Al Avison enlisted the aid of Captain America. Muerte and Tarantula managed to get the drop on Cap knocking him out and throwing him in a river. Captain America recovered in time to capture them before they could carry out their plan, but not before they killed Ken Astor. Philip next turned up helping his brother Jaimie run various casinos. In revenge for killing their brother as well as disrupting their gambling operations it was decided to kill Power Man and Iron Fist. Muerte made several failed attempts to kill them, but all it ended up doing was bringing them to the brothers casino where they were defeated and captured.
abilities: Gambler, highly skilled in the use of knives, expert assassin, average hand-to-hand combatant using basic techniques.
weapons: An assortment of knives, high-powered handguns, hand grenades and flamethrowers concealed in special pockets in his coat and vest.

phillip hart.name: Phillip Hart
phillip hart.first_appearance: Deadly Hands of Kung Fu Vol 1 23
phillip hart.origin: ===Early Life=== From a young age, Phil Hart displayed a fascination with chemistry and propulsion systems, driven by the potential for innovative energy solutions. Excelling in academics, he pursued advanced studies in chemical engineering, delving deeper into fuel efficiency and propulsion technologies. Despite his rigorous studies, Hart found solace and inspiration in playing cards and card games, often using them as a means to unwind and stimulate his strategic mind. During this time, Hart made a groundbreaking discovery – the creation of a revolutionary liquid fuel, "Zero Fluid". This substance promised unmatched efficiency, captivating the scientific community and earning Hart acclaim as a visionary scientist. ===Meeting Marie=== 400px|left|thumb The Contraxian alien race dispatched many scientists to try to discover an energy source to resuscitate the dwindling nuclear processes of the Contraxian sun. Learning of Hart's experiments, one of the alien assumed a totally human form to keep Hart under surveillance. Hart and the alien eventually met, married, and produced a son they named Jack. The alien woman, "Marie," died in a car accident when the boy was a child. Jack grew up without knowing of his mother's origins. right|thumb ===Murder by the Corporation=== When Jack was a teenager, Phillip Hart perfected his "Zero Fluid" and decided to donate the fuel to all the free countries of the world. Hart was then contacted by agents of the criminal Corporation who wanted to market the Zero Fluid. Refusing to deal with them, Phillip Hart was murdered by Corporation agents in front of his son. left|thumb

phillip morgan.name: Phillip Morgan
phillip morgan.origin: Phillip Morgan was a scientist who invented a machine to record sound waves onto solid objects such as rocks and tests the playback on a rock taken from an old temple where the black arts were practiced. At first he hears his voice from the test he made, but then sounds continue as the machine plays back a chant that was stored ages ago on the rock and a demon appears. Actually, it wasn't a demon, but a mutant. The mutant said that the term demon was a deviation from the term mutants were called in the past, which was The Man. Being evil beings, they were trapped in a dimension by sorcerers using a chant, but later another group of evil sorcerers developed another chant that freed them, and that was the one that came out of Phillip's machine. Among the agreements made with the evil sorcerers was that when called they would have to grant a wish before being completely free, and Phillip took the opportunity to ask as a wish that the mutant would return to where he came from, which he was forced to do but disappearing he said that someone else would find the song, so to avoid this Phillips destroyed his machine and communicated that his research on the sound waves that were engraved on every object did not work.

phillip rambow.name: Phillip Rambow
phillip rambow.origin: Professor Phillip Zoltan Rambow was a brilliant scientist who once worked with Reed Richards, who later became Mister Fantastic, leader of the Fantastic Four. Years later, Phillip was working on a device that could neutralize any weapon. Assisted by his son Lawrence. During the experiment something went wrong and Lawrence was bombarded with and transformed by a strange energy. This energy form then went on a rampage across New York City. Not wishing his son to be harmed, Rambow sought out his old colleague, but instead ran into his wife the Invisible Girl, who was fending off the creature during its attack. She was soon joined by her teammates, Mister Fantastic and the Human Torch. Realizing that a neutralizer device in his lab could revert his son back to normal, Rambow was taken there by the Human Torch while Mr. Fantastic and the Invisible Girl kept Lawrence at bay. Getting the neutralizer in on time, Phillip activated it, changing his son back to normal. Following the battle Rambow had to be hospitalized, his subsequent fate is unknown.

philo zogolowski.name: Philo Zogolowski
philo zogolowski.origin: ===Early Life=== Professor Philo Zogolowski was a frail and sickly man born in 1880. As an adult he made a fortune selling his inventions. === 1940s === Professor Zog decided to focus his resources and energy on leaving a positive impact on society and invented the robot known as Electro, hoping to utilize the robot to wipe out crime and corruption. His project was secretly funded by the United States government under the direction of President Roosevelt. He developed his a team of a dozen operatives to work out of his headquarters in the Midwestern United States. Zog gained critical acclaim due to his involvements in the rescue of kidnapped child actress Joyce Lovely, the liberation of the Republic of Molivia from the tyranny of Kalph Belgri, and the elimination of numerous drug cartels including the San Francisco operations run by the Voice. thumb|left|168px|Professor Zog By this time, a hotline was established so that the public could request Electro's aid at any time. Zog sent Electro to deliver aid in a flooding in Ohio, leading to the capture of mobster Boss Sarpo. However, Sapro had his minions kidnap Zog and forced him to use Electro to free Sapro from prison and commit a series of crimes. ===Planet Ligra=== Zog and Electro's crime spree was short lived as they were soon be kidnapped by the Dragon-Men of planet Ligra. On Ligra, Zog was forced to use his invention to attack the Lion-People and capture their ruler Queen Nara. However, Zog freed himself from his Dragon-Men captors and used Electro to turn the tide of battle, slaying the Dragon-Men's leader Jago in the process. Zog was rewarded by being crowned a knight of Ligra before being returned to Earth. ===Crime-Fighting=== Zog's famed work lead to President Franklin Delano Roosevelt requesting Zog deal with the threat of the reanimated corpses of the mad Dr. Bruno Varoz. By this point, Zog had ceased using operatives and took a more active role in Electro's operations. He modified the robot with a televisor that would project the user's face and allow two-way communication between the Electro operator and its environment. With new adaption, Zog came to the aid of his friend John Borden, who's lumber property was being set ablaze by the vindictive Baldwin Drake. Zog once more responded to a request for aid from the president in dealing with the Shark, a notorious pirate. For his aid in destroying the Shark's operations, Zog was awarded a Congressional Gold Medal. Zog accompanied his colleague Dr. Simon Crane and his daughter Betty on a expedition to explore the moon, taking Electro along with him. When Electro was captured by the alien creature called Gnorr. Zog and the others slayed the creature to recover his invention. When a series of strange building collapses prompted the officials of Fairbanks City to call on Zog's assistance, he pit his robot against the subterraneans known as the Onees, slaying their leader. Shortly thereafter, Professor Zog was called to Titan City which was under siege by the evil Dr. Lorrof and his flesh eating "Green Terror". Deducing that the creature' weakness was radium, he slayed the creature with a Radium Gun and Lorroff was slain attempting to unsuccessfully blow up Electro. Zog was once more manipulated to use his robot for crime, this time by Prince Omei, who hypnotized Zog to do his bidding. When Zog suggested to the increasingly paranoid Omei that the authorities might use his lab to build a robot to counter Electro, he ordered Zog to destroy it. Unable to bring himself to destroy his own lab, Zog broke free of Omei's control. With his minions revolting and his plan in shambles, Omei set off a bomb, collapsing the building on all of them. Zog survived thanks to his body being shielded by Electro. When dealing with mystically enlarged animals unleashed by Mor the Mighty, Electro was dismantled by giant birds. Professor Zog would quickly repair the robot and send it after Mor, forcing the magicians plane to crash. Zog saved the Earth from an invasion by the alien Antons from the planet Torsa with the aid of his colleague Dr. Horace Forde. While Electro slaughtered the Anton forces, Zog and Forde used a Magno-Generator to send Torsa away from Earth and detonated the planet with super-bombs. Later, Zog's colleague Sir John Chadwick begged for his help solving a mysterious string of murders directed at his family by a seemingly invisible killer. fields.history: ===Early Life=== Professor Philo Zogolowski was a frail and sickly man born in 1880. As an adult he made a fortune selling his inventions. === 1940s === Professor Zog decided to focus his resources and energy on leaving a positive impact on society and invented the robot known as Electro, hoping to utilize the robot to wipe out crime and corruption. His project was secretly funded by the United States government under the direction of President Roosevelt. He developed his a team of a dozen operatives to work out of his headquarters in the Midwestern United States. Zog gained critical acclaim due to his involvements in the rescue of kidnapped child actress Joyce Lovely, the liberation of the Republic of Molivia from the tyranny of Kalph Belgri, and the elimination of numerous drug cartels including the San Francisco operations run by the Voice. thumb|left|168px|Professor Zog By this time, a hotline was established so that the public could request Electro's aid at any time. Zog sent Electro to deliver aid in a flooding in Ohio, leading to the capture of mobster Boss Sarpo. However, Sapro had his minions kidnap Zog and forced him to use Electro to free Sapro from prison and commit a series of crimes. ===Planet Ligra=== Zog and Electro's crime spree was short lived as they were soon be kidnapped by the Dragon-Men of planet Ligra. On Ligra, Zog was forced to use his invention to attack the Lion-People and capture their ruler Queen Nara. However, Zog freed himself from his Dragon-Men captors and used Electro to turn the tide of battle, slaying the Dragon-Men's leader Jago in the process. Zog was rewarded by being crowned a knight of Ligra before being returned to Earth. ===Crime-Fighting=== Zog's famed work lead to President Franklin Delano Roosevelt requesting Zog deal with the threat of the reanimated corpses of the mad Dr. Bruno Varoz. By this point, Zog had ceased using operatives and took a more active role in Electro's operations. He modified the robot with a televisor that would project the user's face and allow two-way communication between the Electro operator and its environment. With new adaption, Zog came to the aid of his friend John Borden, who's lumber property was being set ablaze by the vindictive Baldwin Drake. Zog once more responded to a request for aid from the president in dealing with the Shark, a notorious pirate. For his aid in destroying the Shark's operations, Zog was awarded a Congressional Gold Medal. Zog accompanied his colleague Dr. Simon Crane and his daughter Betty on a expedition to explore the moon, taking Electro along with him. When Electro was captured by the alien creature called Gnorr. Zog and the others slayed the creature to recover his invention. When a series of strange building collapses prompted the officials of Fairbanks City to call on Zog's assistance, he pit his robot against the subterraneans known as the Onees, slaying their leader. Shortly thereafter, Professor Zog was called to Titan City which was under siege by the evil Dr. Lorrof and his flesh eating "Green Terror". Deducing that the creature' weakness was radium, he slayed the creature with a Radium Gun and Lorroff was slain attempting to unsuccessfully blow up Electro. philoctetes.name: Philoctetes
philoctetes.origin: Philoctetes was the son of King Poeas of Meliboea, and a skilled archer. At some point, he was the comrade of Hercules, and kept his bow and arrows. He was one of the warriors who sailed to Troy to help Menelaus retrieve his wife Helen who had been taken by Troy king Priam's son Priam. While sailing at the isle of Tenedos, where they stopped to feast, Philoctetes was bitten by a viper. Instants later, the wound began to fester and reek. Despite being attended by the healer Aesculapius, the wound kept on reeking, until Philoctetes was left behind on the island of Lemnos to nurse his wound. As the Achaeans departed, he cursed them for abandoning him. After Odysseus learned from Priam's prophetic son Helenus that Troy would not fall until the arrows of Heracles were stroke against its walls, Diomedes went to find Philoctetes, whose wound still reeked. Aesculapius's son Machaon treated the wound, returning Philoctetes to his prime. The next day, during a battle, drawn to the same place by the Goddess Strife, Paris confronted Philoctetes to an archer duel, and Philoctetes, guided by Apollo, killed his rival from one or three arrows. Menelaus rushed to dismember the one who had stolen his wife, but Philoctetes quickly stopped him, letting the Trojans retrieve the body of their prince and take it within the city.
abilities: Philoctetes was a skilled archer, surpassing Achilles, Ajax, and Paris.
weapons: Bow and Arrows of Heracles

phin mason.name: Phin Mason
phin mason.origin: Phin Mason was Miles Morales' best friend and Rick Mason's sister. ===Early Life=== Phin Mason was born on February 21st, 2002. She met Miles at school, when they both disassembled a vacuum cleaner to find out how it worked (to which their school alerted Rio Morales about this) and they became best friends. They used to go around the city stashing time capsules with mementos about their friendship. In one occasion, Miles and Phin created an energy converter with the help of her brother Rick, which won an award at a science convention at the Oscorp Science Center. At some point, Miles and Phin entered an eating competition with a local champion at Coney Island, eating copious amounts of chicken nuggets, only to end up vomiting profusely, though the champion was still impressed enough by their performance that he had the audience give them a standing ovation. Miles later enrolled at Brooklyn Visions Academy and they stopped seeing each other on a frequent basis. thumb|left|Phin with Rick Mason (Earth-1048)|Rick and Miles Morales Sometime in the mid 2010s, she witnessed as Rick, who worked at the Roxxon Corporation became sick as a result of the NuForm, a new component of clean energy that Rick had created for Roxxon. Fearing for the safety of the city and knowing the NuForm's toxic effects on people, both decided to invade a Roxxon testing facility to destroy the a newly constructed NuForm reactor, on May 10th, 2017, by overloading it, in an attempt to stop Roxxon's tests. While helping her brother to deactivate the reactor by hacking into it's systems, they were suddenly interrupted by Simon Krieger, who took back control over the system, trapping Rick inside the overloading reactor, killing him while Phin watched. This left Phin traumatized, swearing revenge on Roxxon and Krieger. ===Becoming the Tinkerer=== After Rick's death, Phin joined a gang called the Underground. She provided them with weapons made of a new kind of programmable matter tech and in exchange, the Underground worked with her to achieve her goals. She then adopted the moniker Tinkerer after a nickname that her brother used to call her when she was a kid. Over time, Phin devised a plan to stop Roxxon and Krieger once and for all. Roxxon had recently built a new Complex Plaza on Harlem, and were planning to instal the first public NuForm reactor at the plaza to power up the entire neighborhood with clean energy. Phin's plan was to boycott Roxxon by stealing a NuForm sample so she could use it to overload the new reactor, blowing up the plaza before it could open for public. thumb|right|Leading Underground (Earth-1048)|The Underground ===War against Roxxon=== In 2020, during Christmas eve, Phin took a break from her plan to finally reconnect with her old friend Miles, when his mother Rio Morales invited Phin and Ganke Lee to spend Christmas at their house. During dinner, Phin overheard as Rio commented about the preparations to her election rally that was about to occur on the next day. Phin then saw the perfect opportunity for a distraction, planning to cause chaos at the rally as a decoy so she could steal the NuForm from a Roxxon shipment that was also about to enter the city through the Braithwaite Bridge on the next day. On the next day, Phin finally put her plan in motion by sending a group of Underground members to wreak havoc on the rally, while she and another group went to the bridge to steal the NuForm from the shipment truck, but things got out of control when Spider-Man appeared to intervene, and accidentally caused the rest of the NuForm shipment inside the truck to become unstable, blowing up the bridge, causing it to slowly fall apart. Phin however, managed to flee from the scene with a NuForm sample. Days later, Phin encountered Miles again at a coffee shop, where he asked her to join the Underground. Unbeknownst to her, Miles was actually Spider-Man. Miles had previously discovered her identity as Tinkerer during their brief encounter at the bridge, and was trying to infiltrate the Underground in an attempt to locate the NuForm sample, and also to discover what Phin had in mind with it. Their friendship gets compromised however, as Phin also discovers that Miles is Spider-Man when he is forced to reveal his identity to her when she almost kills him after a chase through the city. On New Year’s Eve, they decide to meet again at Trinity Church to discuss the state of their relationship after betraying one another with lies, but are interrupted by the Rhino, who was now working for Roxxon and was sent to capture both, sending them to a secret facility underneath New York. While in Roxxon's custody, Phin expresses her disdain by Simon Krieger during interrogation, telling him that she will make him pay for what he did to her brother. She later manages leave the facility, when both Miles are forced to work together to escape, even facing Rhino again. During their escape however, she turns on Miles after he stops her from killing
weapons: Programmable Matter weapons: Phin's technology can morph matter in any shape she desires, be it a sword, hooks, or shields.

phineous umbridge.name: Phineous Umbridge
phineous umbridge.origin: Criminal Phineous Umbridge led five other criminals: Harold, Jonah, Marshall, Maurice, and Peter. In prison, he purchased a magic gemstone from a cellmate. Upon release, he rejoined his associates, but they were injured and arrested. Aboard a police vehicle, Umbridge, with his friends' permission, absorbed their souls into the gem, leaving their bodies dead. When the vehicle hit a pothole, Umbridge inadvertently dropped the gem, which fell from the vehicle and cracked in two near discarded furniture. Harold, Jonah, Marshall, Maurice, and Peter's souls entered a file cabinet, freezer, chair, desk and lamp, respectively. Now virtually indestructible, they attacked bystanders, drawing attention from super-team Excalibur and "the X-Men", the latter actually disguised Warwolves. The groups battled the "Killer Furniture", and Nightcrawler (Kurt Wagner), noticing the broken gem, reassembled it, reabsorbing the five souls. Meanwhile, the Warwolves merged to capture Phoenix (Rachel Summers). They opened a Mojoverse portal, but Shadowcat (Kitty Pryde) rescued Phoenix while Nightcrawler broke the gem, releasing the souls into Warwolves' shared body, which teleported away. The Warwolves later resurfaced, but the souls' fate remains unrevealed. Umbridge was presumably charged with murdering his associates, whose corpses were found in the police vehicle.
abilities: as a freezer and lamp, Jonah and Peter could discharge freezing cold and electricity, respectively.

phinn mac mram.name: Phinn Mac Mram
phinn mac mram.origin: Phinn Mac Mram was a member of his world's Cyber-Sidhe (or "Tribe of Turing"), a race of cybernetic beings native worshipped by the native Mechlans of this Earth, who made sacrifices to them through the ritualistic Henge-Nodes. However, Phinn attempted to enslave the Mechlans, so they rose up against him and banished his warband to another world. Phinn Mac Mram and his warriors re-materialized on Earth-616 at the Carhenge tourist attraction in Western Nebraska. They were engaged by Lyra, acting as an agent of A.R.M.O.R. The Cyber-Sidhe's Chromedruids began infecting Earth's machines and controlling them, including Lyra's wrist-computer, Boudicca. Lyra engaged the Cyber-Sidhe and killed Phinn Mac Mram, ending the Cyber-Sidhe threat.

Along with Helio and Gronk, Phobius infiltrates Attilan and steals a sample, but is captured along with the rest of his team by The Thing and Mister Fantastic.; While they are imprisoned by the Inhuman Royal Family, Maelstrom sends his assassin, Deathurge, to kill Phobius and the rest of the team so they cannot reveal Maelstrom's plan.
powers: Phobius can stimulate the fear center of the brains of humans and animals, manifesting their specific fears.

phoebe marrs.name: Phoebe Marrs
phoebe marrs.origin: Phoebe Marrs grew up with her twin, Desmond, in the shadow of their father, Archimedes Marrs. Archimedes headed Marrs Corp., a struggling corporation. Phoebe longed for a simple, quiet life and at age 19, she ran away to the Midwest and met Michael Payne. They fell in love and married where Phoebe spent the next 18 months as a happy housewife. When Michael's business collapsed, he began to struggle with feeling useless. Desmond showed up and offered Michael a million dollars to divorce Phoebe, which he accepted. Phoebe later realized that Desmond's hand had been in Michael's business failings as well. Three months later, Phoebe found out she was pregnant and took a world cruise after Desmond ordered Phoebe to have an abortion. After her son Edward was born in Singapore, she had him secretly brought back to the states and found a house in Connecticut where new employees Sumner and Miss Wickham could raise him in secret. She kept her son a secret from Desmond and the media. After their father died, the Marrs twins struggled to balance their inheritance. They sought out the financial aid of Headhunter, a business woman who required her clients to sign a contract that would allow her to collect their 'head' years later. Desmond and Phoebe signed away, never thinking Headhunter would actually collect. thumb|Phoebe with her brother Desmond Under the leadership of the Marrs twins, the Marrs Corporation became very successful. The Marrs Corporation were at odds with Anthony Stark of Stark Enterprises as they fought over corporate holdings. Stark beat the Marrs in buying out a company called Centrex, causing Desmond to retain a hatred for Stark. Seeking revenge on Tony Stark, Kearson Dewitt approached Desmond and Phoebe with a plan to take Stark down. Dewitt designed a chip that would be implanted in Stark's spine that would allow the paralyzed Stark to walk again but that would, in time, give Dewitt direct control over Stark's nervous system. The Marrs twins agreed to fund the project. One evening, Phoebe returned from a business trip in Hong Kong and grew angry with employees. She went to Desmond's apartment and Bevis, the butler, directed Phoebe to Desmond's location in the gun room. She found Desmond ready to shoot himself, and deflected the gun just in time. She renewed Desmond's interest in life by turning him on to the challenge of ferreting out the mystery man behind the new Oracle, Incorporated. Finding out the identity of this mysterious benefactor became Desmond's sole reason for living. Desmond hired Griffin to attack Carrie Alexander, one of Oracle's proxy buyers in an attempt to identify the true owner. Namor was exposed as the mysterious benefactor. Desmond constructed a plan to destroy Namor. As part of Desmond's plan, he wanted Phoebe to seduce Namor. When she expressed concern that Namor may be too mighty a foe for them, Desmond slapped Phoebe to silence her. In an attempt to get the two to meet, Desmond pushed Phoebe off the roof, leaving Namor to catch her. After Namor did so, Phoebe kissed him in gratitude. Namor returned Phoebe to her home and she slipped into a bathrobe. Phoebe charmed Namor briefly, then received notice of Sluj, an ecological disaster, attacking a Marrs ship, the Sea Queen. When Desmond learned that Namor had gone off to investigate the Sea Queen, he was furious. He grabbed Phoebe as if to hurt her, and was shocked when Headhunter came in stating that it was time to collect. After Namor defeated Sluj, Phoebe rushed to him, asking for help against Headhunter. In the back of her limo, she confided in Namor, then kissed him. Phoebe and Namor confronted Headhunter, demanding Desmond's return, and Phoebe wondered if another arrangement could be made (offering Namor as a trade for Desmond), but Headhunter informed them it was too late as Desmond was already mounted on her wall. Later, after Namor had defeated Headhunter and Desmond had been freed, Phoebe watched the news about Headhunter's defeat. Namor went to Marrs Corp. to confront Phoebe on her betrayal, and Desmond acted shocked and appalled at Phoebe's behavior in front of Namor. Namor left thinking Phoebe cold and ruthless and Desmond full of honor. Phoebe grew frustrated with Desmond's laughing over Namor's folly. She began to realize that perhaps she really did love Namor. thumb|Phoebe checking up on Dewitt Desmond and Phoebe went to check on Dewitt in the Stark project. When they arrived, Dewitt was noting how Stark seemed to be exerting a high amount of physical activity (as Iron Man, though they did not know this). Desmond, fearing Stark would injure himself, had them shut down Stark's nervous system. Desmond reasserted his power over Dewitt, at one time bending Phoebe's wrist to get her to stand away. After Phoebe reminded Desmond what a worthy opponent Stark was, Desmond agreed to let Kearson continue running the project and departed. Kearson tried to flirt with Phoebe, but she denied his advance and left. Stark Enter
abilities: She is a shrewd and talented business woman accustomed to ruling a multi-billion dollar company.

fields.trivia: John Byrne has acknowledged that Desmond and Phoebe Marrs were heavily inspired by Mel and Susan Profitt, characters on the 1980s television series Wiseguy. Like Susan Profitt, Phoebe Marrs becomes romantically involved with the hero of the series, and following her brother's death is consumed by the delusion that he is still alive. Phoebe Marrs has been the subject of two major retconned plot points. In , Headhunter comes to collect Phoebe's head, but in the following issue, it is retconned that Headhunter came for Desmond instead. Second, in , Phoebe Marrs is confronted by the Punisher in her limo. The scene ends there, leaving the reader with the implication that Phoebe is murdered by the Punisher, but evidently John Byrne decided he had more use for Phoebe or simply forgot about this scene, because in the next issue Phoebe appears, still alive, and does not even mention her encounter with the Punisher, much less explain how she survived.

phoenix 1 000 000 bc.first_appearance: Generations: The Unworthy Thor & The Mighty Thor Vol 1 1
phoenix 1 000 000 bc.origin: ===Origins=== As an infant, Firehair was abandoned by her parents at the "Burnt Place" - a permanently razed clearing where the xenophobic surrounding tribes sacrificed anyone who deviated in any way from their norms - due to her red hair. Rescued by a pack of wolves, she grew up as a member of the pack - occasionally returning to the Burnt Place to chase the giant buzzards that dwelled there. When she was ten, Firehair discovered a child with one eye had been left at the Burnt Place, and was confronted by a floating man who spoke to her with his mind. Initially fleeing in fear, she later followed the man out of curiosity and befriended him, learning that he could only communicate via telepathy and move using psychokinesis. Reluctantly leaving her pack, Firehair joined the Tribe Without Fear - a collection of mutants that the man - who Firehair called the Highwalker - had rescued from the Burnt Place and taken upon himself to raise and train. ===Lady Phoenix=== Some time later, Firehair's own mutant abilities awakened just in time for her to warn the Highwalker of an impending attack by the neighboring xenophobic tribes. As Highwalker attempted to talk down the tribesmen to buy his charges time to escape, Firehair's newly awakened psychic abilities were overwhelmed by the humans' fear and rage, resulting in the Highwalker's death when he dropped his guard to soothe her. Firehair fainted as her fellow pupils gave into rage and attacked the attacking tribesmen, resulting in the deaths of everyone present save herself. Firehair blamed herself for her mentor and friends' deaths and was overcome with despair, contemplating turning her powers on herself to commit suicide and returning to the Burnt Place to be eaten by the buzzards. As she lay awaiting death, the Phoenix Force - who had created the Burnt Place when it first arrived on Earth - manifested and saved her from the buzzards. Drawn to Firehair's untapped raw psychic power, the Phoenix bonded to her and sought to use her to fulfill its intended purpose - razing planets to ashes. Consumed by vengeful rage, Firehair nearly gave into the firebird's bloodlust and became a Dark Phoenix, but was pacified by the wolf who had saved her as an infant and decided to use her powers to protect those weaker than herself rather than destruction. Years later, Firehair recruited the Asgardian deity Odin Borson - intent on forming an alliance with other supernatural and mystically-augmented beings. Together, she and Odin recruited the demigod sorcerer Agamotto, the Black Panther - chief of the Panther Tribe, the demonically-empowered Ghost Rider, Fan Fei - first wielder of the Iron Fist, and Vnn - bearer of the cosmic Starbrand. One of the most-powerful enemies the Avengers battled was the Fallen, an out-of-control Celestial who unbeknownst to them was corrupted by the Horde. During the Avengers' battle against the corrupted cosmic god, Firehair struck the Fallen with flames hot enough to melt a supernova, but it withstood her attack without as much as a scratch. The Avengers eventually defeated the Fallen and sealed in an underground chamber in what would become the modern-day country of South Africa. Afterwards, Firehair and her allies battled the First Host sent to judge Earth, and went on to face many other threats to the Earth; the devil Mephisto and his minions, time-travelling would-be despots, and a young Thanos among them. thumb|left|Firehair and Starbrand sacrificed themselves While she was romantically involved with Odin, Firehair rejected him after his callous reaction to the Black Panther's death. When Odin later tried to force her to marry him, Firehair left Earth never to return. Surviving their allies by thousands of years, Firehair served as Gaea's midwife during Thor Odinson's birth. When the newborn Thor was assassinated by Laufey, Firehair resurrected him and imbued him with some of the Phoenix's power - Gaea declaring her Thor's second mother. Some time after, she sensed the battle between the Multiversal Masters of Evil and the Avengers of the future, among them being Thor. She then traveled to Earth, before following the two teams to the God Quarry, where she battled the Dark Phoenix. Following the battle with Mephisto at the Quarry of Creation, Firehair and Starbrand sacrificed themselves to restore the universes decimated by the Council of Red's machinations, Firehair's essence being preserved inside the White Hot Room with the other Phoenix avatars. ===Legacy=== The Phoenix Force kept Firehair's consciousness suppressed in the White Hot Room, but she nevertheless exerted a degree of subconscious influence over it - causing it to instinctively seek out hosts from Earth - with a preference for red-haired women with psionic abilities. As such, Firehair proved to be the first of many human mutants to host the Phoenix Force, with Jean Grey, Rachel Summers, and Hope Summers following in her footsteps. fields.personality: As a child, Firehair was initially feral - having been raised by a pack of wolves. Sensing a kindred spirit in the Highwalker, she reluctantly left the only family she had known behind and became one of his pupils. When the awakening of her own mutant powers unintentionally caused the deaths of the Highwalker and her friends, Firehair became suicidally depressed until she was found by the Phoenix Force. Upon bonding to it, Firehair gave in to her rage and hatred, embraced the firebird's bloodlust, and vengefully set out to raze the world as a Dark Phoenix. Pacified by the wolf that had saved her as an infant, she instead chose to dedicate herself to protecting humanity both from itself and from malevolent supernatural forces. As an adult, Firehair enjoyed teasing her comrade and lover Odin over his initial inability to control the recently-forged Mjolnir. Despite using her powers for good, she possessed a love of combat and destruction, suggesting to Odin that she could immolate anyone and anything who stood in their way with her cosmic flames. She and Odin remained comrades and lovers for some time after the other Stone Age Avengers perished. Her consciousness through the Phoenix Force seemed caring and protective of her son and said she wished for more time with Thor, everything she's doing is for the betterment of the future world for Thor and if she survives the storm that's coming, she will tell Thor everything.
fields.notes: Firehair and her tribe were allegedly "mutants" from 1 million years ago, though this conflicts with preestablished mutant history and also implies that Homo superior predated Homo sapiens. However, explains the existence of modern humans in the 1,000,000 BC era by stating that some humans fell into a chronal rift. This may also explain Firehair and her tribe. The traditional explanation for the latent superhuman potential in humanity was the First Host from 1 million years ago. However, a retcon gave that role to the Progenitor over 4 billion years earlier.

phoenix messiah demon.species: Alien Demon ascended as the Phoenix Messiah in order to take down the Lords of Stasis and launch back Evolution and Progress, later invested with the Phoenix Force
phoenix messiah demon.origin: ===Evolution stopped=== A billion years ago, the demonic rulers of an unknown planet performed a great rite in order to bring evolution and progress to halt, so that they could enslave their planet's population. ===The Messiah and the Lights=== The rite proved to be effective, until the Phoenix Messiah emerged. After emerging, she gathered five acolytes, the Lights, who banded together to destroy the rule of the demon lords. All of them were powered beings, but their origins are unknown. Together, they waged war against the Lord of Stasis, and at last, the Phoenix Force came to their planet, and communed with the Messiah and her Lights. ===Evolution restarting=== The spell was broken by the Five and One through the Phoenix Force, and the Demons were swept away. The whole history was witnessed by the alien peace-keeping robot Unit. When he encountered another Phoenix Messiah a billion years later, he intended to deprive her of her own Lights to see what would happen.

phondath.name: Phondath
phondath.origin: In the times of elder Hyperborea, giant reptiles known as the Dragon Kings ruled Earth, including Lemuria. That time was known as the Age of Dragons. Among those giant reptiles rose kings and necromancers, the Dragon Kings, who had a wicked and cruel way of life. They built monolithic cities of black stone, and studied the dark arts. Witnessing the Dragon Kings' evil, the Nineteen Gods created the first men: Phondath the Firstborn and his mate Evalla. Phondath became a hero, known to ride his mythical winged dragon.

phough.name: Phough
phough.origin: Phough was the leader of the Troll Associates. After failing to capture Alchemy due to the interference of X-Factor, he sent them into hiding for a few years, before re-emerging and kidnapping Alchemy's mother Ophelia. He then captured Alchemy and used him to create them vast amounts of gold, and turn their enemies into gold as well. He managed to capture both Excalibur and the X-Men with enchanted chains, but Nightcrawler convinced him that he was on their side, letting him go and fight two of his teammates, Feron and Cerise. After pretending to fight them, Nightcrawler challenged Phough to single combat, and when Phough tried to cheat, Alchemy turned him to gold and undid the transformations of the other heroes.

weaknesses: Like all trolls, Phough was sensitive to bright .

phraug.name: Phraug
phraug.origin: Phraug was emperor of the Deviant empire Lemuria 20,000 years ago. Under his rule the Deviants had conquered most of the Earth with only Atlantis holding out. Phraug sent his forces against Atlantis, but the Atlanteans destroyed themselves rather than be conquered. At about the same time the Celestials returned to Earth and believing them to be a threat Phraug ordered them fired upon. As this was happening Atra, Lemuria's chief alchemist, approached Phraug with the newly created Serpent Crown. Atra intended to use the Crown to destroy Phraug and take over his empire, but Phraug was a worshipper of Set and immune to the effects of the Crown. Phraug and Atra fought over the Crown as the Celestials retaliated, firing upon Lemuria and causing its destruction. Lemuria was sunk, but Phraug and Atra's skeletons were somehow preserved still holding the Crown.

phy.name: Phy
phy.origin: Phy was the leader of the Troll Associates, a group of trolls that lived in England before the rise of civilization. One day, after smelling gold, he discovered the mutant Thomas Jones aka Alchemy, who possessed the power of matter transmutation. After learning of Alchemy's power, Phy came up with a plan to crash England's economy by flooding the market with an influx of gold created using Alchemy's power, allowing trolls and other magic folk to take over. After Phy kidnapped Alchemy, Alchemy's mother Ophelia contacted X-Factor to rescue her son. X-Factor's interference forced Phy and his troll ally Phee to flee with Alchemy. After threatening to kill Alchemy's mother, Alchemy decided to turn Phy and Phee into gold. On advice from X-Factor, Alchemy turned Phy and Phee into lead and were placed in Hyde Park as statues, where they likely remain in the present time.

phyla.name: Phyla
phyla.origin: ===Odyssey=== Phyla-Vell was created as a genetically-engineered offspring of the legendary Kree warrior Captain Marvel and the beast tamer from Titan created by I.S.A.A.C. known as Elysius. Her conception was carried out as a replication of the process that had created her older brother, Genis-Vell. As such, she was artificially aged into adulthood. This all happened following Genis-Vell recreation of the universe, during which he remade himself more heroically and competent, ultimately inspiring his mother Elysius to envision a sister for him. Unlike Genis-Vell, Phyla-Vell was raised in Titan fully aware of her origins. She was trained by Elysius into becoming a better warrior than her older brother, being given a pair of artificial Nega-Bands replicas that acted as redistributors of energy and inheriting a limited version of the Cosmic Awareness. 180px|thumb|left|Phyla-Vell becomes Captain Marvel The actions of the insane Genis-Vell's across the universe forced Elysius to reveal herself to stop him. Recognizing Genis-Vell was no longer worthy of bearing the name of his father, Elysius blessed Phyla-Vell with the mantle of Captain Marvel and assigned her to defeat her brother. During the confrontation, Genis-Vell had glimpses of memories of a sister he had never met. Ultimately, he realized the nature of the reality disruption involving the crisis and transported himself, Phyla-Vell and Elysius to the Nth Space. Elysius took the opportunity to force Genis-Vell to confront his instability as the result of his immaturity. In desperation, he repaired his mind and swore not to cause additional harm. Phyla-Vell was frustrated with her broken-spirited brother being celebrated as a champion despite his failures. She wished for Genis-Vell to fully relinquish the name of Captain Marvel to her so she could restore its glory. Genis-Vell traveled to the future to investigate the course of events leading to the corruption of Marlo Chandler, the wife of his partner and ally Rick Jones. Before departing, he asked Phyla to protect the present-day Marlo Chandler, who was living in Los Angeles and was romantically involved with the psychic from Titan Moondragon. Chandler ended up becoming a target of the evil being known as the Magus, prompting Phyla-Vell to prevent a kidnapping attempt. Given the assault, Phyla-Vell decided to protect Chandler in Titan, a decision Moondragon supported. In fact, the Magus targeted Moondragon and psychologically tortured her, drawing Phyla-Vell's attention. After Genis returned and Chandler's future was secured, Moondragon informed Chandler that she had subconsciously used her telepathy to enamor her. Phyla-Vell could immediately recognize Moondragon lied to preserve Chandler's marriage with Jones. Believing the selfless attitude to be honorable and attractive, Phyla-Vell invited Moondragon to explore the galaxy with her, something the telepath gladly accepted. ===Annihilation Wave=== 180px|thumb|right|During Annihilation On Titan, Starfox was accused of using his pleasure power immorally without others' consent. Phyla-Vell and Moondragon supervised the trial to confirm either his ill actions or his innocence. A witnessed summoned to the ordeal was the former teammate of Starfox, She-Hulk. Upon learning he had used his powers on her without her knowledge, She-Hulk went on a rampage, leading Phyla-Vell to physically intercept her. The fight was interrupted by Thanos, the Mad Titan and deadly nemesis of Captain Marvel. Through Moondragon's telepathy, Thanos was revealed as an imposter, and Starfox's innocence was proven. As Captain Marvel, Phyla-Vell joined the last assault against the duplicate of Thanos. Genis-Vell was killed in action, and Elysius informed Phyla-Vell about his fate. She took the opportunity to express how both her children were disappointments compared to their honorable father. Overtaken by grief and a sense of inferiority, Phyla-Vell could not see herself worthy of carrying on the legacy of Captain Marvel. She visited her brother's and her father's graves alongside with Moondragon, who counseled her to move past their shadows. The couple of cosmic heroes was surprised by the real Thanos, who captured Moondragon and easily overpowered Phyla-Vell. He advised Phyla-Vell to alert Moondragon's father, Drax the Destroyer, about his hostage's situation to prevent an intervention. Disturbed, Phyla-Vell found Drax accompanied by the girl from Earth Cammi Benally in Daedalus 5. Phyla-Vell asked for him to join her in rescuing Moondragon, but Drax could only worry about his very reason of being, ending Thanos. Amidst this difficult situation, Phyla-Vell became part of the United Front led by Peter Quill, the legendary Star-Lord, and Rich Rider, the man called Nova, against the Annihilation Wave invasion. Led by Annihilus and subtly influenced by Thanos, the Wave brought terrible losses across the universe, and the survivors had to retreat. Feeling like the war was otherwise lost, N

phyty.name: Phyty
phyty.origin: During the events of the Superhuman Civil War, Phyty was present when the Sentry unexpectedly arrived on the Moon seeking refuge from the conflict. As a telepath of the Inhuman Royal Court, she was tasked with examining the Sentry’s mind to determine his intentions and evaluate the potential danger he represented. Upon entering his thoughts, Phyty witnessed one of the Sentry’s distorted internal narratives—an imagined past adventure in which he believed he had fought alongside the Inhuman Royal Family against the Red Ronin. Although the memory held no basis in reality, it provided the Inhumans with insight into the Sentry’s unstable mental state. Phyty’s assessment played a key role in shaping the Royal Family’s cautious response to his presence.

fields.unusual_features: Phyty has a non-human facial structure typical of certain Terrigen-mutated Inhumans, with pronounced ridges and an altered cranial shape.

piaka loio.name: Piaka Loio
piaka loio.origin: The Piaka Loio was the orphaned son of a prostitute in Naou. He met a man named Seivi while trying to beg him for money. Impressed by the persuasiveness of the young boy, Seivi, and the child worked together and created an elaborate cult of personality around the child. Claiming he was the Piaka Loio, the reincarnation of a Naouan god Baru, Seivi became the boy's general and they rallied a small army to oppose the ruling Prime Minister of Naou and the royal family. Elektra Natchios was hired by the Prime Minister to assassinate the mysterious Piaka Loio, who never appeared publically. When she discovered the Piaka Loio was a child, Elektra's conscience would not allow her to murder him. Instead, she killed the entire army, leaving no one behind who knew the face of the Piaka Loio. With his cult gone, the Piaka Loio was found by the Naouan army. They were unimpressed by the child's "tall tales" of being the famous revolutionary and made him a ward of the state.

fields.history: The Piaka Loio was the orphaned son of a prostitute in Naou. He met a man named Seivi while trying to beg him for money. Impressed by the persuasiveness of the young boy, Seivi, and the child worked together and created an elaborate cult of personality around the child. Claiming he was the Piaka Loio, the reincarnation of a Naouan god Baru, Seivi became the boy's general and they rallied a small army to oppose the ruling Prime Minister of Naou and the royal family. Elektra Natchios was hired by the Prime Minister to assassinate the mysterious Piaka Loio, who never appeared publically. When she discovered the Piaka Loio was a child, Elektra's conscience would not allow her to murder him. Instead, she killed the entire army, leaving no one behind who knew the face of the Piaka Loio. With his cult gone, the Piaka Loio was found by the Naouan army. They were unimpressed by the child's "tall tales" of being the famous revolutionary and made him a ward of the state.
